Public announcement

Public announcement

A four-minute announcement, hard and direct, built to cut through a street. It opens on the record itself, then says what the report is, what it concludes, how it grades every claim, and what you do now. Free to download and play.

One pass · 3:55 · a low sting opens each section

Playing it

  • Set the loop to repeat, or play the hour file straight through. Each pass is complete on its own, so anyone walking past hears all of it within a few minutes.
  • Check the local rules on amplified sound before playing it in public. Many cities limit volume and hours, or require a permit.
  • If you adapt the words, keep “What this is not.” Federal law, 18 U.S.C. § 2387, makes it a crime to urge members of the armed forces toward insubordination or refusal of duty. That section is what keeps the announcement clear of it.

The words

Who this is from

This is a public announcement.

It comes from a private citizen. It is not from the government, and it is not from the police.

It is about crimes that institutions were told about, and a record that is still being kept dark.

The record

In nineteen ninety-six, a woman reported Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell to the police, and was sent on to the FBI. Nothing happened for a decade.

In two thousand and seven, federal prosecutors signed a deal. It gave immunity to co-conspirators the government had not even named.

After a sex-offence conviction, he kept his access to the powerful for another ten years.

In two thousand and nineteen, he died in federal custody, awaiting trial.

Ghislaine Maxwell was convicted. She is serving twenty years.

And the record is deliberately dark. A review declared closed. Some two hundred thousand pages withheld or redacted. Reports kept under seal.

What the report is

There is a report that puts that record in one place, with its sources named.

It is free. It is public. And every line of it can be checked.

Read it online. b0b.dev.

It starts with Epstein and Maxwell. Then it follows the money, the surveillance, the forced labour, the wars, and the files that are still withheld.

What it concludes

On one question, the report commits.

Its conclusion is this. Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell functioned as deniable assets: an intelligence-useful role, under civilian cover.

That is a judgment on the documented record. It is not a document, and the report says so.

It makes no claim that either of them was run by a handler. And it tells you what would bring its conclusion down.

How it works

Every claim in the report carries a grade. Documented. Attributed. Labeled. Contested. Unsupported.

It prints what it could not prove. It publishes its own corrections.

It asks you to check it, not to trust it.

What you do now

So here is what you do.

Read it. Choose one claim. Check its source.

If it is wrong, prove it, and send the correction.

If it holds, say so. Tell one person. Today.

To anyone who serves

To anyone who serves. In uniform. In an agency. In law enforcement.

What the report documents has no hands of its own. Every capability runs because trained people operate it. People like you.

Your duty is to obey legal orders. Under military law, obeying a clearly illegal order is no defence.

This message does not ask you to disobey legal orders. It does not ask you to desert, to sabotage, to obstruct, or to leak.

If you see wrongdoing, use the lawful channels: an Inspector General, or a Member of Congress.

For service members, federal law forbids reprisal for that. Title ten of the United States Code, section ten thirty-four.

Wherever you serve, there is an oversight route. Use it. And do not send classified material to anyone.

Close

The report opens with a line from the Gospel of John. For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.

The record already exists. The only question left is whether it is read honestly.

This has been a public announcement, from a private citizen.

The report is online. b0b.dev.

How it was made

The voice is synthetic: Piper’s en_GB-cori-high, a model trained on public-domain LibriVox recordings. The sting between sections and the low pulse under the voice are synthesised; nothing is sampled, and neither sounds like an alert tone, a siren or a blast. The address to anyone who serves is adapted from the report’s own, To those inside.

Before publishing, a speech-recognition model transcribed one pass as rendered and through four simulated street recordings: a small speaker at a distance, with traffic noise six, then three, decibels below the voice. In noise it got about 95% of the words right, and every sentence whose meaning rests on a negation (“makes no claim”, “does not ask you to disobey legal orders”, “do not send classified material”) was heard with the negation intact, every time.
